nodes.description: Constructor of GamerGirlCrypto: sets name, symbol, decimals, _totalSupply and credits the deployer with the whole supply.
totalSupply(): returns _totalSupply - balances[address(0)] using unchecked arithmetic in totalSupply.
balanceOf(address tokenOwner): returns balances[tokenOwner].
allowance(address tokenOwner, address spender): returns allowed[tokenOwner][spender].
approve(address spender, uint tokens): writes allowed[msg.sender][spender] and emits Approval.
transfer(address to, uint tokens): debits balances[msg.sender] via safeSub and credits balances[to] via safeAdd, emits Transfer.
transferFrom(address from, address to, uint tokens): debits balances[from] and allowed[from][msg.sender], credits balances[to], emits Transfer; missing allowance require check is implied by safeSub.
SafeMath.safeAdd(uint a, uint b): c = a + b; require(c >= a).
SafeMath.safeSub(uint a, uint b): require(b <= a); c = a - b.
SafeMath.safeMul(uint a, uint b): c = a * b; require(a == 0 || c / a == b).
SafeMath.safeDiv(uint a, uint b): require(b > 0); c = a / b.
Public string state variable holding the token name 'GamerGirlCrypto'.
Public string state variable holding the token symbol 'GGC'.
Public uint8 state variable holding token decimals (18).
Public uint256 _totalSupply holding the total token supply (1e27) set in the constructor.
Internal mapping(address => uint) balances tracking token ownership; written in constructor, transfer and transferFrom.
Internal mapping(address => mapping(address => uint)) allowed tracking ERC20 allowances; written in approve and transferFrom.
msg.sender in the constructor; used as the key receiving the entire initial supply and as Transfer event argument.
msg.sender in approve(); controls the owner slot of the allowed mapping and the Approval event.
msg.sender in transfer(); controls which balance is debited.
msg.sender in transferFrom(); used as spender key in allowed[from][msg.sender].
Unchecked subtraction _totalSupply - balances[address(0)] in totalSupply(); underflows if address(0) holds a balance.
Addition a + b inside safeAdd guarded by require(c >= a).
Subtraction a - b inside safeSub guarded by require(b <= a).
Multiplication a * b inside safeMul guarded by require(a == 0 || c / a == b).
Division a / b inside safeDiv guarded by require(b > 0).

edges.reason: Constructor assigns the literal token name to the name state variable.
Constructor assigns the literal token symbol to the symbol state variable.
Constructor assigns the decimals value 18 to the decimals state variable.
Constructor assigns the initial 1e27 supply to _totalSupply.
Untrusted msg.sender is used directly as the key that receives the entire initial balance, so the deployer identity controls ownership.
The initial _totalSupply is written into balances[msg.sender].
totalSupply() reads _totalSupply as the minuend of the unchecked subtraction.
totalSupply() reads balances[address(0)] as the subtrahend of the unchecked subtraction.
The unchecked subtraction result is returned by totalSupply(), so an underflow would propagate as the reported supply.
balanceOf uses the tokenOwner parameter as the lookup key into the balances mapping.
balanceOf returns the value read from the balances mapping.
allowance uses tokenOwner as the first-level key of the allowed mapping.
allowance uses spender as the second-level key of the allowed mapping.
allowance returns the value read from the allowed mapping.
approve writes allowed[msg.sender][...] using the untrusted caller address as the owner key.
approve uses the spender parameter as the second-level key of the allowed mapping.
approve stores the tokens parameter as the allowance value in the allowed mapping.
transfer debits balances[msg.sender], letting the untrusted caller choose which balance is reduced.
The caller-controlled balance balances[msg.sender] is passed as argument a to safeSub.
The tokens parameter is passed as argument b to safeSub in transfer.
safeSub result is written back into the balances mapping.
transfer uses the to parameter as the key of the credited balance balances[to].
The destination address to is used to read balances[to] before calling safeAdd.
The tokens parameter is passed as argument b to safeAdd in transfer.
safeAdd result is written to balances[to], completing the transfer credit.
transferFrom debits balances[from] using the caller-supplied from address.
balances[from] is passed as argument a to safeSub in transferFrom.
The tokens parameter is passed as argument b to safeSub for both the balance and allowance debits.
transferFrom writes allowed[from][msg.sender], using the untrusted caller as the spender key that authorizes the allowance spending.
The from parameter is used as the first-level key of the allowed mapping in transferFrom.
The tokens parameter is subtracted from the stored allowance in the allowed mapping.
transferFrom uses the to parameter as the key of the credited balance balances[to].
The destination address to is used to read balances[to] before safeAdd in transferFrom.
The tokens parameter is passed as argument b to safeAdd in transferFrom.
Parameter a of safeAdd is the left operand of the guarded addition.
Parameter b of safeAdd is the right operand of the guarded addition.
The addition result is assigned to the local variable c in safeAdd.
The local c is the named return value of safeAdd.
Parameter a of safeSub is the left operand of the guarded subtraction.
Parameter b of safeSub is the right operand of the guarded subtraction.
The subtraction result is assigned to the local variable c in safeSub.
The local c is the named return value of safeSub.
Parameter a of safeMul is the left operand of the guarded multiplication.
Parameter b of safeMul is the right operand of the guarded multiplication.
The multiplication result is assigned to the local variable c in safeMul.
The local c is the named return value of safeMul.
Parameter a of safeDiv is the numerator of the guarded division.
Parameter b of safeDiv is the denominator of the guarded division.
The division result is assigned to the local variable c in safeDiv.
The local c is the named return value of safeDiv.
transfer() calls safeSub to debit the sender balance before any other state change.
transfer() calls safeAdd to credit the destination balance.
transferFrom() calls safeSub twice: once for the sender balance and once for the allowance.
transferFrom() calls safeAdd to credit the destination balance.
totalSupply() directly executes the unchecked subtraction, which is a core arithmetic risk when balances[address(0)] is non-zero.

normalization_plan.reason: The tokenOwner parameter only exists to index balances inside balanceOf, so it can be normalized into the balanceOf function node.

The tokens parameter is stored directly as the allowance value by approve, so it merges into the approve function node.

The tokens parameter is only used as the transfer amount inside transfer and can be folded into the transfer function node.
The from parameter is only used as a balances/allowed key inside transferFrom and can be folded into the transferFrom function node.
The to parameter is only used as a credited balances key inside transferFrom and can be folded into the transferFrom function node.
The tokens parameter is the transferFrom amount and allowance debit amount, so it folds into the transferFrom function node.
